response_text:
Claim 1 (currently amended): (Currently Amended) A cell comprising: a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide, wherein the non-native compartment is formed by the self-assembly of the proteinaceous shell in vivo.

Claim 8 (currently amended): (Currently Amended) The cell of claim1any preceding claim wherein the proteinaceous shell comprises a plurality of different BMC polypeptides, wherein the plurality of different BMC polypeptides comprises BMC polypeptides from different bacterial species and from different BMC operons.

Claim 12 (currently amended): (Currently Amended) A method comprising: introducing into a host cell a polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide, thereby producing a transformed cell; and growing the transformed cell under conditions effective for the transformed cell to express the polynucleotide that encodes at least one BMC polypeptide and produce a non-native compartment comprising a proteinaceous shell comprising the at least one BMC polypeptide, wherein the method is used for enhancing metabolic processes in the host cell.

Claim 21 (currently amended): (Currently Amended) A method comprising: providing a cell comprising a non-native compartment comprising: a proteinaceous shell comprising at least one bacterial microcompartment (BMC) polypeptide, and at least one enzyme that catalyzes conversion of a substrate to a product, wherein the method is used for producing a desired product; and growing the cell under conditions effective for the at least one enzyme to catalyze conversion of the substrate to a product.
